R cells run in [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/), a build of R for the
browser. Real Quarto runs R through knitr; the playground imitates knitr's
output, producing the same markdown and cell attributes as Quarto's knitr
hooks, so cell options, figures and cross-references render the way they do
in Quarto.

webR downloads the first time a playground on the page has R code. After
that, every playground on the page shares one R session, and each render
starts with a fresh environment, as a new `quarto render` would.

## Cell options and output

````{quarto-simulator}
#| height: 520
---
title: "Cars"
---

```{r}
speeds <- cars$speed
summary(speeds)
message("A message, shown like knitr shows it")
warning("And a warning")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cars
#| fig-cap: "Stopping distance increases with speed."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
plot(cars, pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
```

The fastest car went `{r} max(speeds)` mph. @fig-cars shows all
`{r} nrow(cars)` cars.

```{r}
#| error: true
log(-1)
stop("This error is shown because of `error: true`")
```
````

Supported cell options:

- `echo` (including `echo: fenced`), `eval`, `include`, `output` (including
  `output: asis`), `warning`, `message` and `error`
- `label`, `fig-cap`, `fig-alt`, `fig-width` and `fig-height`, also set for the whole
  document under `execute:` or at the top level
- `code-fold`, `code-summary`, `code-line-numbers` and `code-overflow`
- `classes`, `column`, `panel` and `layout-ncol`/`layout-nrow`
- Header options in knitr style, such as ```` ```{r label, echo=FALSE} ````

Inline code, `` `{r} expr` ``, is evaluated in the same environment as the
cells. To show a cell verbatim, fences included, double the braces:
```` ```{{r}} ````.

## Errors

Without `error: true`, an error stops the render, as in Quarto. The message
says which cell failed and which lines, and suggests `error: true`:

````{quarto-simulator}
#| height: 260
---
title: "Broken"
---

```{r}
x <- c(1, 2, 3)
mean(y)
```
````

## Packages

`library()`, `require()` and `pkg::fn()` install packages on first use from
the [webR package repository](https://repo.r-wasm.org/), which builds most
of CRAN. The status line shows the progress. Large packages take a while the
first time, so this playground waits for **▶ Render**:

````{quarto-simulator}
#| autorender: false
#| height: 460
---
title: "ggplot2"
---

```{r}
#| label: fig-mpg
#| fig-cap: "Fuel economy by engine size."
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = class)) +
  geom_point()
```
````

## Differences from knitr

- **Plots** are drawn on webR's canvas device and shown as PNG images. Each
  plot appears after the last expression that drew on it, as with knitr.
- **Printing** follows R's own `print()`. Rich output from packages that use
  `knit_print()` methods (for example `knitr::kable()` tables) prints as text.
- **Not available:** reading local files, `cache`, `child` documents, other
  knitr engines (`bash`, `sql`), and `htmlwidgets`.
- **Infinite loops** can't be interrupted. The learner has to reload the page.
  Interrupting webR needs cross-origin isolation headers on the site.
